findings.fix: Change the color to a darker shade such as #333333 or #666666 to achieve sufficient contrast.
findings.violation: Gray text (#999999) on a white background fails WCAG contrast requirements, making it difficult to read and especially inappropriate on a transit accessibility page.

findings.fix: Change the label's for attribute from "topic-alt" to "topic" to match the select element's id.
findings.location: Section "Weekend service", form label for Route field (s3-form-topic-label)
findings.violation: The label's for attribute references "topic-alt" but the select input has id="topic", breaking the label-input association.

findings.fix: Remove both the height and overflow styles, or change overflow to "auto" to allow scrolling if the content exceeds the height.
findings.violation: Fixed height with overflow:hidden will truncate any content taller than 60 pixels, potentially hiding important status information.

findings.fix: Replace with a native `<button>` element, or add JavaScript event listeners to handle keyboard interactions.
findings.violation: A div with role="button" does not natively handle Enter or Space key presses required for keyboard accessibility.

findings.evidence: `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">` followed by `<span class="error-text" aria-live="polite" id="s3-form-promo-error">`
findings.location: Section "Weekend service", promo code input and error message (s3-form-promo-error)
findings.violation: The invalid input is not connected to its error message; screen reader users won't know which message describes this field's error.

findings.fix: Change the link text to "read the fare history" or update the href to point to the actual accessibility improvements page.
findings.location: Section "Weekend service", link to adjustments list (s3-link1)
findings.violation: The link text "accessibility improvements list" does not match the destination "/fares/history", creating confusion about where the link leads.
